Determine a set of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ that generate the above parabola. Express your answer in the form $x=2pt,y=p{t}^{2},$ where $p$ is a constant.

feedback.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(0,0),$ and passes through the point $(4,2).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola  that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=2pt,\,y=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(4,2),$ we can substitute $x=4$ and $y=2$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}4=2pt \\ 2=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2pt \\ 2 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{2}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =p{(\frac{2}{p})}^{2} \\ 2 & =p\cdot \frac{4}{{p}^{2}} \\ 2 & =\frac{4}{p} \\ p & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=2(2)t,\,y=(2){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=4t,\,y=2{t}^{2}.
$$
